_comment: Real response shapes from live calls to web.archive.org during story 9.1
(2026-10-16), not invented. Two things were confirmed live and matter for
how app/ingest/campaign_sites.py treats this API:
1. `GET /wayback/available?url=...` -- the 'availability' lookup -- is
genuinely free and keyless. A live call for https://www.congress.gov/
returned exactly the 'available_response' envelope below (status 200).
This can only report an EXISTING snapshot; it cannot trigger a new one.
2. Save Page Now itself (the capture-TRIGGERING endpoint,
POST /save/<url> with Accept: application/json) is NOT free/keyless for
programmatic use, contrary to this story's brief. A live call with no
credentials returned exactly the 'unauthenticated_response' envelope
below -- HTTP 401, 'You need to be logged in to use Save Page Now.' The
plain (non-JSON) GET /save/<url> a logged-out browser session would use
was also tried live and returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited guest access,
confirmed by the 'x-rl: 0' header on the real response) with no
snapshot produced -- also captured below as 'rate_limited_response'.
So this module treats Save Page Now as OPTIONAL and best-effort: it is
attempted only when SPN2 credentials are configured (an access/secret
key pair from a free archive.org account, per the official SPN2 docs),
and a failure of any kind -- 401, 429, timeout, or no credentials
configured at all -- degrades to 'not archived on Wayback this run'
rather than failing the capture. The 'success_response' envelope below
is the documented shape SPN2 returns to an authenticated caller (per
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Nsv52MvSjbLb2PCpHlat0gkzw0EvtSgpKHu4mk0MnrA,
fetched live during this story) -- held as a fixture only, since no
archive.org account credentials exist in this environment to confirm
it against a real authenticated call. See the module docstring.

body.message: You need to be logged in to use Save Page Now.
